label: copy-phase input i (strongest when the token being output next is f)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never during original input or at <DEL>), almost always when the fed-back input is the letter i (96% of activation mass); a small remainder fires on input f, mainly right after an i was copied. Not every copy-phase i fires: whether it fires, and how strongly, depends on the original token that follows the i, i.e. the token being output at this step. Firing rates are highest when that token is f (~99% precision, the max activations are all i->f), then p/s/i/r/d/x/j/n/a/u/3; they are intermediate for b/c/h/o/0/1 (~40-47%) and near zero for w/k/e/2/y/t. Magnitude is also higher at early recall positions (recall_idx 1-3). Plain (phase==2)&(in_tok==i) gives dev F1 0.61 with mass recall 0.96; restricting to the high-rate set of next tokens gives F1 0.70 with mass recall 0.78. The next-token dependence is graded, not a clean set, so the feature is only partially explained.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: i, f, d, s, -, r; least: m, c, b, 3) and the token being output, by phase (copy phase: f, i, s, p; input phase: ; delimiter step: ); timing cues that raise it most: t=10, L=9 & t=10, L=9 & t=11.
